title: Kinkéliba Tisane
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: A big handful of kinkéliba leaves added to a litre of boiling water, covered and boiled about 15 minutes, left to infuse and sweetened to taste — or cooled with a few drops of lemon.
longDesc: Amina Savoura’s ‘Kinkéliba en tisane’, published on Afrik on 27 January 2013, is the cleanest kinkéliba method found. A litre of water is brought to the boil and the kinkéliba added; the pot is covered and boiled about 15 minutes; it is left to infuse and served sweetened to taste. For variety it can also be infused with a few leaves of lemongrass or mint, or finished with a few drops of lemon and drunk cold. The method is a covered boil — a decoction — despite the word ‘infuser’. THE ONLY MEASURE FOR THE LEAVES IS ‘UNE GROSSE POIGNÉE’ (a big handful), a vernacular volume not converted to grams; the lemon, lemongrass or mint carries no quantity. The one peer-reviewed study of Dakar preparation (Moussa et al. 2017) confirms it is a decoction of dry Combretum micranthum leaves but, in the part of it that could be read, gives no leaf quantity, water volume or time.
ingredients: 1 big handful kinkéliba leaves (une grosse poignée) — not weighed in the source
Lemon (optional), or lemongrass or mint leaves — quantity not printed
steps: Bring the water to the boil and add the kinkéliba leaves.
Cover and boil for about 15 minutes.
Leave to infuse. Serve, sweetened to taste.
For variety, infuse it with a few lemongrass or mint leaves, or add a few drops of lemon and drink it cold.
chefTips: The only cue is the timer, ‘environ’ 15 minutes; the infusion has no endpoint.
It is a decoction — a covered boil.
Add the lemon after cooking, not in the pot.
commonMistakes: Treating the handful as a precise measure.
Uncovering the pot, which loses aroma.
reheating: Served hot, or cold with lemon.
healthBenefits: Kinkéliba is ‘réputé pour ses nombreuses vertus, en particulier digestive’ (the page’s wording); this is tradition, not a medical claim.
culturalNote: ‘Utilisée dans la plupart des pays du Sahel … la préparation de boisson à base de Kinkéliba donne souvent lieu à de véritables cérémonials.’
sources: Title as printed: «Kinkéliba en tisane». Byline: «Amina Savoura», Afrik (afrik.com), category Culture. «Publié le 27 janvier 2013 à 23h00». Yield: none printed (4 used for scheduling). TWO-PASS, identical both passes.

Cues: none beyond the timer: «laissez bouillir 15 minutes environ»; «Laissez infuser» with no endpoint. ABSENT: weight of the leaves; quantity of lemon, lemongrass or mint. The prep and rest figures are scheduling estimates.

Background (not used for quantities): Moussa, Diallo, Ndiaye and Sadji (2017), AJFAND 17(4), 12534–12546 — ‘Kinkeliba herbal tea is made of a decoction of dry leaves of Combretum micranthum’; the full text with quantities could not be fetched. The page metadata lists only one creator against four authors in the citation; both reported.
